name: GutsMan's attack's spawn's r3, each game's leftover
why: BN4's third-kind spawn (0x080032F0 through 0x08003210) stores the caller's r1, r2 and r3 at the object's +0x34, +0x38 and +0x3C and r4 at +4, as BN6's twin through the dispatch's spawner does; GutsMan's spawner of his attack's 0x1C (0x080D0894: push {r0,r1,r2,r5}; movs r0,#0x1c; the spawn) sets r0 alone, so +0x3C holds what r3 held before it: in BN4 the battle state's pointer, in BN6 3. No code of the 0x1C object reads +0x3C (its init 0x080D057C and update 0x080D058E and the routines they reach, walked by tools/xnavirecipe_bn4.py), nor do the engine's routines it calls
